title: Cancellation, Minimum Holding and Reinstatement Terms
content:
Terms on which an Optional Supplemental Benefit Rider may be brought to an end, and on which one ended for non-payment may be taken back up.

| Rider | Months the rider must be held before it may be cancelled | Rule turning a cancellation into an end date | A rider terminated for non-payment may be put back in force |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ridgecrest Preventive Dental Rider | 0 | the last day of the month in which the request was received | yes |
| Ridgecrest Vision Plus Rider | 0 | the last day of the month in which the request was received | yes |
| Ridgecrest Hearing Advantage Rider | 3 | the last day of the month in which the request was received | yes |
| Ridgecrest Comprehensive Dental Rider | 6 | the last day of the month in which the request was received | yes |
| Ridgecrest Premier Dental Rider | 12 | the last day of the month in which the request was received | no |
| Ridgecrest Dental Vision Hearing Bundle Rider | 12 | the last day of the month in which the request was received | no |

## The three terms

**Minimum holding months.** The months the rider must be held before it may be cancelled.

**Cancellation effective date rule.** The rule that turns a cancellation into an end date. It is the same on all six riders: the last day of the month in which the request was received.

**Reinstatement.** Whether a rider terminated for non-payment may be put back in force.

## Note on the schedule

The minimum holding period rises across the schedule from 0 months on the Ridgecrest Preventive Dental Rider and the Ridgecrest Vision Plus Rider, through 3 months on the Ridgecrest Hearing Advantage Rider and 6 months on the Ridgecrest Comprehensive Dental Rider, to 12 months on both the Ridgecrest Premier Dental Rider and the Ridgecrest Dental Vision Hearing Bundle Rider.

Those same two riders at 12 months are the two that permit no reinstatement; the other four permit it.
